look: In the old city: tall stone and brick houses with wooden window screens called mashrabiya, the minarets of hundreds of mosques, and narrow lanes. To the west, a new quarter of wide European-style streets built from the 1860s.
Men in long robes called galabiyas, with turbans or the red felt fez. Women outdoors in black cloaks and face veils.
On foot, by donkey (donkey boys hired them out like taxis), camel and horse carriage.
Oil lamps in the old lanes, gas lamps in the new quarter.
Egypt was still part of the Ottoman Empire on paper, but British troops had occupied it since 1882 and British officials ran the country.

stops.name: A street in the old city
stops.title: Cairo, street in the Arab quarter
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: A slender stone tower of a mosque. Cairo was called the city of a thousand minarets.
spots.how: Many medieval minarets still stand in old Cairo.

spots.d: Mashrabiya: carved wooden screens that let in breeze and let people look out without being seen.
spots.how: You can see them sticking out over the street.

spots.d: Small shops open to the street under cloth and wooden awnings.
spots.how: Cairo's old markets still work like this.

spots.d: A man in a white turban and long robe walks toward us.
spots.how: Most men in the crowd are dressed the same way.

stops.name: A public fountain
stops.title: Cairo, fountain in the Arab quarter
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: A public fountain. Rich Cairenes paid for these so passers-by could drink for free.
spots.how: Its big windows with gold metal grilles are where the water was handed out.

spots.d: Another minaret rises above the lane.
spots.how: Mosques stood on almost every street of old Cairo.

spots.d: Women outdoors wore long black cloaks and veils.
spots.how: Photographs and travellers' books of the time show the same.

stops.name: Barbers in the street
stops.title: Cairo, Arab barbers in the street
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: The customer checks his shave in a round mirror.
spots.how: Street barbers worked sitting on the ground on mats.

spots.d: Turbans wrapped around a small cap.
spots.how: Almost every man here wears one.

spots.d: A street lamp in a newer square of the city.
spots.how: Gas lamps were spreading in Cairo's newer streets.

stops.name: Street sellers
stops.title: Cairo, street sellers
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: Food and goods were sold from carts and trays all over the city.
spots.how: Street selling is still a big part of Cairo life.

spots.d: The cart rolls on two big wooden wheels.
spots.how: Pushed by hand through lanes too narrow for horses.

spots.d: A seller in a white turban and blue robe.
spots.how: Blue cotton was cheap and common.
